question: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2000 as a sum borrowed at 8% per year rate of interest for 4 years.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective rate of Simple Interest = Rate × Time

Effective Rate = 8% × 4 = 32%

Simple Interest = 32% of Principal

Simple Interest = (32 ÷ 100) × 2000 = ₹640

**∴ The correct answer is ₹640.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹2000

Rate (R) = 8% per year

Time (T) = 4 years

 Total Simple Interest = ₹640

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = (2000 × 8 × 4) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 20 × 32

⇒ SI = ₹640

**∴ The correct answer is ₹640.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Amount in Simple Interest

The total amount paid at the end of the time period is Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI). It can also be written as A = P [1 + (R × T) ÷ 100].

Simple vs Compound Interest

Simple Interest is calculated only on the principal amount, whereas Compound Interest is calculated on the principal and the accumulated interest. CI formula: CI = P(1 + R ÷ 100)T − P.

Difference between CI and SI

For exactly 2 years, the difference between CI and SI on a sum is calculated using the shortcut formula: D = P × (R ÷ 100)². For 3 years, it is D = P × (R ÷ 100)² × (3 + R ÷ 100).
